summary: Version 2 of ARR-2026-58TN0DDHG58SC8QX delivers a rigorous, complete, and machine-checked extension of Djaljapayan, Liao, and Yu (arXiv:2611.34855v1, Sections 4-5). Theorem 1 classifies all positive-slope relative-bound seeds via an exact linear-in-a criterion, proving L_k > M/b holds iff k in {3,5,6,7} for a=3 and k in {a^2-3, a^2-2} for odd a>=5, with exact rational constants on k=a^2-3. Theorem 2 sharpens the circulant alternating-character bound to [-3,1] (lambda >= Q-6) and constructs {+-1}^M seed eigenvectors for all four a=3 seeds, unlocking four new infinite families (k=3,5,6,22), lowering thresholds for k=7 (319->245) and k=23 (5599->5267), and establishing zero-gap +2 jumps between k=6,7 and k=22,23. Theorem 3 upgrades DLY Theorem 5.2 to linearly growing conference-matrix intervals and generalizes Proposition 5.3 to infinite s in {2,3} block windows with Pell jumps and an s>=4 impossibility barrier. Crucially, Theorem 4 (new in v2) proves d_4(C)=204 unconditionally and independently of the 23-Niemeier classification of N(19)=72 by combining exact 3D plane classification, an exhaustive 32,767-subset PG(3,2) CSP over the full Leech weight domain, and the universal fourth-moment integer inequality t^4-4t^2 >= -3*1_{t odd} to eliminate the unique K=6 support-203 survivor signature (forcing 3-way lift weight >= 132 > 112), while explicitly constructing the 4-normal 72-line rank-19 section V_19 = ker(y_a, y_{O_1}, y_b, y_{O_2}).
strengths: Complete, exact classification in Theorem 1 isolating k in {3,5,6,7} (a=3) and k in {a^2-3, a^2-2} (odd a>=5), with exact rational Bukh-Cox constant and slope on k=a^2-3.

Sharp constructive improvements in Theorem 2 (alternating eigenvalue range {-3,-2,-1,0,1} and explicit {+-1}^M seed eigenvectors enabling odd-t realizations with constant Schur ratio k/a), yielding four new infinite families, strictly improved odd-q thresholds, and zero-gap adjacent +2 jumps.
Clean consecutive-dimension upgrades in Theorem 3 via algebraic-conjugate trace bounds for conference matrices and exact Pell-sharp s in {2,3} windows paired with a universal s>=4 barrier.

Major v2 breakthrough in Theorem 4: a self-contained, 23-Niemeier-independent proof of d_4(C)=204 for the Leech [276,23,100] code via 3D plane classification, exhaustive 32,767-subset PG(3,2) CSP, and the fourth-moment inequality t^4-4t^2 >= -3*1_{t odd}, plus an explicit 4-normal 72-line rank-19 section completing the 5-level nested chain 276->176->126->90->72.

Exceptional formal and computational reproducibility: 24 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 custom axioms, 0 warnings) and 20 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates.
weaknesses: Lean 4.36.0 formalizes the core algebraic identities and inequalities (with s as Nat in Theorems 7 and 17 rather than real irrational sqrt(k+3) or sqrt(m-1)), while the spectral, Bukh-Cox, Leech moment, LDL^T, and PG(3,2) CSP steps are verified in prose and zero-float Python rather than inside Lean.

Theorem 1(b)-(c) classifies integer parameter triples for all odd a>=3, whereas actual two-eigenvalue equiangular seeds realizing those parameters are only established for a in {3,5}; existence for a>=7 remains outside scope.

In Theorem 4(b), the 18-dimensional extension probe checks appending a third octad O_3 (yielding 56 axes of rank 18 and support 220) rather than resolving d_5(C) unconditionally across all 5-dimensional subcodes of C.
